title: Time2pack
cardSummary: From one travel-prep app to two products with a clear focus each: Time2Pack for organising a trip and OnlyFlights for following flights.
sub: Two connected travel apps. Time2Pack helps people organise a trip, and OnlyFlights grew out of it into a standalone app for flights — I shaped the product decisions, flows and interfaces as both grew.

cover.alt: Time2Pack trip screen on a phone standing on a rock against the sky

sections.heading: Overview
sections.headline: From one travel-prep app to two focused products
paragraphs: I worked as the product designer on two connected travel apps. Time2Pack helps people prepare a trip: packing lists, notes and documents. OnlyFlights grew out of it into a standalone app for flights.
My job was to grow the functionality while keeping the interaction simple: product decisions, new features, reworked flows and screens, A/B test data and development constraints.

sections.heading: The challenge
sections.headline: More capability without losing a simple structure
paragraphs: Preparing for a trip is a pile of small tasks: packing, checking the weather, keeping documents, following flight details. They belong to one trip, but each comes up at a different moment and needs a different level of attention.
As Time2Pack grew, the question became how to add capabilities without losing a clear purpose.

sections.heading: 01 — The key decision
sections.headline: Flights got an app of their own
paragraphs: Flights needed a focus of their own, so we moved them out into a separate app. Each product got a clear job.

steps.title: Time2Pack
steps.text: Prepare and organise the trip: packing lists, notes, documents and the overall travel context.

steps.title: OnlyFlights
steps.text: Keep flight information at hand: add flights, check status, times and details.

sections.heading: 02 — Time2Pack
sections.headline: A shorter path to the main task
paragraphs: We dropped the complex onboarding and shortened the creation flows, so people take fewer actions before they can start using the app.

steps.title: Cards on the trip screen
steps.text: Weather, packing, notes and documents are split into clear blocks.

steps.title: Progress at a glance
steps.text: The packing card shows how many items are checked off out of the total, without opening the list.

steps.title: Two ways to add a document
steps.text: Take a photo or upload a file.

sections.heading: 03 — OnlyFlights
sections.headline: Making a flight readable
paragraphs: Flight screens carry a lot of data: route, times, status, flight number, terminal, gate. I reworked how it is grouped and how the hierarchy reads, and the flight card became the main element of the overview.

steps.title: A delay says what changed
steps.text: A text status, colour highlight and the new time next to the crossed-out original.

steps.title: Check-in stands apart
steps.text: Online check-in is a prominent action, set apart from the reference details.

steps.title: Depth where it is needed
steps.text: Later versions added a route map and expandable information about the operating carrier and related flights, keeping secondary data away from the main route.

sections.heading: 04 — Visual system
sections.headline: One system, two products
paragraphs: Time2Pack uses a purple accent and OnlyFlights a blue one, built on shared principles: cards, rounded surfaces, repeatable information blocks and clear primary actions.

Both apps have light and dark themes, so status, primary text, secondary data and actions had to stay distinguishable in each. Each component was designed with its states in both themes: empty, focused and filled inputs, collapsed and expanded blocks, and the locked Pro state.

sections.heading: 05 — Beyond the app screens
sections.headline: Widgets, watch and the App Store
paragraphs: I designed home-screen widgets for the phone, where space is tight and the choice of content matters most.

steps.title: Live Activities
steps.text: Several states of the flight card in dark and light, shown on the lock screen: countdown to departure, terminal and gate, seat, weather at the destination.

steps.title: Watch widgets
steps.text: Two sizes, large and small, showing flight progress and the departure and arrival dates. They change with the stage of the flight, and the layout is adapted to each size.

steps.title: App Store screenshots
steps.text: People do not know the product yet, so the sequence shows what it can do and why they might need it.

sections.heading: 06 — Trade-offs
sections.headline: Feasibility is part of the design
paragraphs: I studied A/B test data and joined product discussions, but development effort shaped the decisions too. Some ideas turned out far more complex to build than they looked in design, and we dropped several of them.

sections.heading: Reflection
sections.headline: Growth means cutting, too
paragraphs: A growing product needs its complexity reviewed regularly. Every new feature affects navigation, hierarchy and the first steps, so growth meant not only adding functions but also cutting flows, revisiting decisions and giving flights an app of their own.

result: Two focused products instead of one overloaded app: Time2Pack for preparing a trip and OnlyFlights for following a flight. Time2Pack has grown into a travel companion used by tens of thousands of people worldwide.
